data.title: Kinetic Energy Explorer
data.description: Investigate how quadratic dependence on velocity versus linear dependence on mass influences the total kinetic energy of a moving system.
data.context: Classical mechanics relating the mass and velocity of a macroscopic object to its translational kinetic energy.

parameters.name: Mass
parameters.description: The inertial mass of the translating object.

parameters.name: Velocity
parameters.description: The instantaneous linear velocity of the object relative to an inertial reference frame.

observations.trigger: Isolate mass (m) by holding velocity constant and incrementally doubling the mass value
observations.prompt: Examine how the kinetic energy scales in direct proportion to the mass. Consider why doubling the mass results in a strictly linear increase in energy, whereas altering other parameters may yield non-linear consequences in classical mechanical systems.

observations.trigger: Isolate velocity (v) by locking the mass and exponentially increasing the velocity parameter
observations.prompt: Analyze the parabolic trajectory of the kinetic energy output as velocity increases. Explain the physical significance of the squared velocity term in the equation and discuss why high-velocity impacts present exponentially greater destructive potential than low-velocity impacts.

challenges.instruction: Calculate the translational kinetic energy of a macroscopic object when its mass is increased to 20 kg, maintaining the default velocity of 5 m/s.

prediction.explanation: Using the kinetic energy formula E_k = 0.5 * m * v^2, substituting m = 20 kg and v = 5 m/s yields E_k = 0.5 * 20 * (5)^2 = 10 * 25 = 250 Joules.

challenges.instruction: Determine the resulting kinetic energy if the velocity of the default 10 kg mass is increased to 10 m/s.

prediction.explanation: Using the kinetic energy formula E_k = 0.5 * m * v^2, substituting m = 10 kg and v = 10 m/s yields E_k = 0.5 * 10 * (10)^2 = 5 * 100 = 500 Joules.

challenges.instruction: Compute the kinetic energy for a reduced mass of 4 kg while keeping the velocity at its default value of 5 m/s.

prediction.explanation: Applying the formula E_k = 0.5 * m * v^2 with m = 4 kg and v = 5 m/s gives E_k = 0.5 * 4 * (5)^2 = 2 * 25 = 50 Joules.

challenges.instruction: Evaluate the kinetic energy for the default 10 kg mass when its velocity is adjusted to 4 m/s.

prediction.explanation: Applying the formula E_k = 0.5 * m * v^2 with m = 10 kg and v = 4 m/s gives E_k = 0.5 * 10 * (4)^2 = 5 * 16 = 80 Joules.
